The SF SPCA recruits adult volunteers (info session, six-month commitment) for dog walking, cat socialising, fostering and mobile vaccine clinics.
Refuse Refuse - San Francisco Cleanups runs weekly KEEP Ocean Beach cleans and monthly Crissy Field and Fort Miley cleanup days; Save the Bay also runs volunteer shoreline restoration.
East Bay Dipping Society holds group ocean dips and Alameda Open Water Swimming meets weekly, but no dedicated ice-bath venue was confirmed.
Alemany Farm in the Excelsior holds community workdays where volunteers garden and harvest.
Fort Funston in the Golden Gate National Recreation Area is widely used as an off-leash dog park, the only GGNRA park allowing off-leash dogs.
Meetup lists many hobby groups and events across San Francisco and the East Bay.
Kabuki Springs & Spa offers Eastern, Swedish and prenatal massage alongside its Japanese-inspired bathhouse.
San Francisco Zen Center's City Center is an urban temple offering zazen practice, beginner resources and a calendar of classes and retreats.
826 Valencia in the Mission runs after-school programs, workshops and in-school projects staffed by volunteer tutors and mentors for students aged 6-18.
Kabuki Springs & Spa describes a Japanese-style bathhouse with natural thermal spring soaking in the city; the natural springs of Calistoga and Sonoma are well beyond 30 km.
Kabuki Springs & Spa is a Japanese-inspired bathhouse with communal baths in Japantown, an approximation of an onsen using heated pools rather than a volcanic source.
SF Parkour has listed free monthly beginner 'Urban Ninja' sessions with rotating locations including the Embarcadero and UC Berkeley, but no dedicated gym in the city was confirmed.
Maddie's Pet Adoption Center at the SF SPCA Mission campus offers walk-in, same-day cat and dog adoptions for adults with photo ID and proof of address.
Club Pilates Alameda runs Reformer Pilates classes with a full weekly schedule.
San Francisco Buddhist Center runs a Saturday morning qigong and meditation session, and other Bay Area venues list qigong sessions.
Sports Basement Stonestown hosts a weekly Wednesday evening Stonestown Run Club, and other free run clubs meet at stores and venues across the city.
Kabuki Springs and Spa in Japantown offers a communal Japanese-style bathhouse with a cedar dry sauna, steam room and hot and cold pools open daily.
NAMI San Francisco runs free peer-led support groups and classes for people with mental health conditions and their families (English, Spanish, Cantonese).
The Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco in Chinatown listed weekly Chen-style Tai Chi classes taught by Master Debbie Au (page may be dated).

how: San Francisco Zen Center (City Center) offers zazen meditation, chanting, dharma talks, classes and retreats, plus beginner resources.
The Sutro Baths ruins, Point Lobos tunnel and Fort Miley gun batteries can be explored on foot, and the Parks Conservancy has led historian walks there.
The San Francisco-Marin Food Bank takes volunteers for warehouse and community shifts; sign-up is online.
Berkeley Yoga Center (open since 1997) runs ongoing classes for beginners through advanced practitioners.

California outlawed bullfighting in 1957; only bloodless Portuguese-style bullfights are allowed at religious festivals in the Central Valley (for example around Thornton), roughly 130-150 km and 2 hours east, May to October.
Nearest cable wakeboard park found is Velocity Island in Woodland, Yolo County, outside the Bay Area; 2015 source.
Canyoning needs slot canyons with flowing water, which the Bay Area lacks; the nearest guided canyoning is in the Sierra Nevada foothills, around 3 hours' drive.
No developed or open caves in the Bay Area; the nearest guided cave and spelunking tours are at Moaning Cavern in the Sierra Nevada foothills (Calaveras County), roughly 3 hours' drive east.
Trap and skeet field inside city limits at a long-running gun club by Lake Merced; the club has faced closure pressure so status should be checked.
Mild coastal climate with no snow; nearest dog sledding is around Lake Tahoe/Truckee, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours by car.
No glaciers in the region; the nearest are on Mount Shasta, roughly 5 hours north, or in the high Sierra.
A city Recreation and Park Department and Outward Bound California high ropes and aerial challenge course in John McLaren Park, reported to open to community members on monthly community days.
venue: Outward Bound California ropes course (McLaren Park)

how: No luge or bobsled track in Northern California; nearest dedicated tracks are in Park City, Utah, or Lake Placid, New York.
No alpine terrain in the metro area; nearest mountaineering is in the Sierra Nevada, roughly 4 to 5 hours by car.
Open-air tandem skydives from 18,000 ft at a drop zone in Byron, roughly an hour east; no drop zone in the city.
Tandem paragliding from the sea cliffs at Mussel Rock, about 15 minutes from the city; hang gliders and paragliders also fly Fort Funston.
The Grand National Rodeo is held annually each autumn at the Cow Palace on the San Francisco-Daly City boundary, with professional rodeo events plus trick riding.
No desert dunes in the metro area; the nearest sandboarding is at Oceano Dunes about 4 hours' drive south, or desert dunes in Southern California.
Carpeted ski-deck treadmill lessons for carving, with a mandatory one-hour intro class for first-timers.
No snow or ski slopes in the Bay Area; nearest ski resorts are around Lake Tahoe, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours by car.
No suitable volcano nearby; the standard site is Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, a long-haul flight away.
No suitable whitewater rivers in the metro area; nearest commercial rafting is on the American River near Coloma, roughly 2 to 2.5 hours away.
Redwood canopy zipline tours in Occidental, Sonoma County (about 90 minutes north) and Mount Hermon in the Santa Cruz Mountains.
